label: Query C (Defective Product)
query: I was injured because of a defective product.

applicable_laws.explanation: Harm Caused To Him On Account Of A Defective Product

engine.rights_explanation:
Based on the legal context provided from The Consumer Protection Act, 2019:

Under Section 84 of the act, if you were injured due to a defective product, the manufacturer of that product may be liable for your harm. This liability exists even if the manufacturer can prove they were not negligent or fraudulent in making any express warranty about the product.

The relevant Act and Section citations are:
- **Act**: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
- **Section**: Section 84 - Harm Caused To Him On Account Of A Defective Product

engine.rights_explanation:
According to Section 17 of The Code on Wages, 2019, your employer is required to pay you within two working days after termination of employment. Since you have not received your wages post-termination, this indicates a potential violation of the law.

Section 45 of The Code on Wages, 2019, outlines the procedure for recovering unpaid wages if an employer fails to comply with Section 17. Specifically, if your employer has not paid your wages upon termination, you may approach the appropriate authority who will issue a certificate of recovery to the Collector or District Magistrate. They are then responsible for recovering the unpaid amount as arrears.

Please refer to Sections 17 and 45 of The Code on Wages, 2019.
